summary.one_liner: Docker templates and launcher script for self-hosting the Discourse open-source discussion forum platform.
summary.what_it_does: The repository provides Docker configuration for deploying a Discourse forum, with templates and a base image that set Discourse's recommended defaults. A bash script named launcher manages containers: it can bootstrap, start, stop, restart, enter, view logs for, rebuild, and clean up containers based on YAML config files. The README describes a standalone template that bundles everything into one container, and a multi-container setup (data.yml and web_only.yml samples) that separates services for easier upgrades, scaling, and redundancy. Config files support composed templates, port exposure, volume mounts, links, environment variables, labels, and hooks. Email must be configured through the SMTP_URL variable, since the image does not include an MTA.
use_cases: Deploy a discussion board on my own server
Run a multi-server Discourse setup for scaling or redundancy
Manage Discourse containers with a launcher script
Run a forum behind a proxy
how_to_run: Read the install guide linked from the README (the standalone template is the recommended starting point)
Copy a template from the samples directory into the containers directory
notable: Standalone template installs Discourse in one container, reportedly in 30 minutes or less
Multi-container layout allows rebuilding web containers while the site stays up
Launcher script handles bootstrap, rebuild, enter, and cleanup commands
Config files can compose child templates and run hooks before or after build steps
Shared directory keeps uploads and logs outside containers so they survive rebuilds
caveats: Email must be set up separately via SMTP_URL; the image contains no mail server
Multi-container setups need a firewall (e.g. ufw or iptables) to protect postgres and redis ports
Multi-container setup is more complex than the standalone template
README mentions Discourse hosting services as a paid option
